in_arabic.name: عُبيد

in_urdu.name: عُبید

data.cultural_impact: The name Ubayd holds a significant cultural impact throughout the Islamic world as it is rooted in the rich history of the Prophet Muhammad's companions (Sahabah). One of the most famous companions bearing this name is Ubayd ibn Umayr ibn Abd al-Muttalib (R.A.), who is recognized for his valiance and bravery during the early Islamic battles. Ubayd's name holds a symbolic connection to the sense of presence and dedication, which has been passed down through generations as a source of inspiration and pride.
data.spiritual_significance: In the spiritual context, the name Ubayd signifies one who is present before God and His Prophet, emphasizing the importance of constant remembrance, obedience, and serving as a true servant to the Divine Creator. The name is also a reminder of the Prophet's saying, "The best thing a servant can say is: 'O Allah, I am present.' So Allah says, 'I am also present, and I have prepared a reward for him.'" (Bukhari and Muslim). The name Ubayd, therefore, holds a deep spiritual significance, highlighting the essential components of submission to God and the importance of being present in both the physical and spiritual realms.

historical_references.reference: Ubayd ibn Harith, the first governor of Kufa under the Rashidun Caliphate. He played a significant role in the early Islamic conquests and was a companion of Prophet Muhammad.
historical_references.context: Ubayd was appointed as the governor of Kufa, a major military and administrative center in Iraq, by Caliph Umar ibn Al-Khattab. He led the defense of Kufa during the siege by the Byzantines and Sassanians in 633 AD, and played a crucial role in the Islamic conquest of Syria under the command of Khalid ibn Al-Walid. His leadership and administrative abilities were vital in the establishment of the early Islamic state in Iraq.

historical_references.reference: Ubayd Allah al-Mahdi, the fifth caliph of the Fatimid Caliphate in North Africa. He was known for his religious learning and military prowess.
historical_references.context: Ubayd Allah al-Mahdi was the third son of Caliph Al-Mu'izz li-Din Allah. He assumed the caliphate after his father's death and led several military campaigns to expand the Fatimid empire in North Africa and Egypt. He was also a learned scholar of Islamic law and jurisprudence and is considered one of the most pious and just caliphs in Fatimid history.
